answer: Cross-epoch **pulse consistency gate**: each identity records a coarse activity fingerprint per epoch (timing histogram, counterparty mix). At each **summit** of the epoch cycle, the verifier checks that the fingerprint's drift stays inside a tolerance band; identities exceeding it enter probation and lose routing weight until drift converges. An attacker cloning identities must sustain plausible drift across many epochs, forcing per-clone history maintenance—a **saffron**-flagged cost: every clone needs genuine ongoing participation, so marginal cost scales linearly, not to near-zero.
